title: Buffered 0.30-day blocks reverse the exponential-tail model advantage for the known D1268 Kepler dip
abstract: We test a narrow exponential dust stream on three known deep dips of KIC 3542116 in Kepler release 25. A finite stellar chord and exposure average separate crossing time from tail time. The forward profile gives lower prediction error than its reverse in both flux products for all three events, when four sets of 0.15-day blocks are withheld and refitted. Its error is also lower than that of a split Gaussian with the same number of shape parameters in all six short-block comparisons. However, 0.30-day blocks with a 0.05-day buffer reverse that advantage for D1268 in both products. The forward-tail errors are 404.5 and 403.0 ppm, versus 348.9 and 367.0 ppm for the split Gaussian. D992 and D1176 retain the forward-tail advantage. Thus, D1268 model ranking depends on the withheld-data rule. We provide all scores, sensitivity fits, numerical checks, source hashes, raw files, and offline code. The scores test local interpolation and have correlated errors. They do not prove a dust cause or establish a new body. No independent telescope confirmation is supplied.
